item.title: Trauma care performance and patient outcomes - insights from a major trauma centre in Sweden.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma, Penetrating, Prehospital, Systems/QI] [strong match]
Eriksson J, Larsson E, Arnason B et al.

PURPOSE: Trauma is a leading cause of death among individuals under 45 years of age. Evaluating trauma system performance over time is important but inherently difficult due to concurrent changes in patient demographics, case-mix and care processes. The aim of this study was to describe temporal changes in patient demographics, injury severity and trauma care at a major trauma centre in Sweden from 2017 to 2023. We hypothesised that risk-adjusted 30-day mortality decreased and that time to computed tomography was reduced over the study period.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Karolinska Trauma Registry, including all trauma patients aged > 15 years fulfilling criteria for full trauma team activation, admitted between January 2017 and August 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess changes in 30-day mortality over time, adjusted for age, sex, injury severity category, ASA score and injury type. Time from arrival to computed tomography was analysed by linear regression and, because the distribution was skewed, by quantile (median) regression.

RESULTS: A total of 5,615 trauma patients were included. Over the study period, the patient population became older, and ASA scores increased, while injury severity and the proportion of penetrating injury remained unchanged. In multivariable logistic regression with 2017 as reference, the odds of 30-day mortality in 2022-2023 were lower (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88, P = 0.008) after adjusting for confounders. Median time to computed tomography decreased from 31 to 21 min; the adjusted difference in 2022-2023 compared with 2017 was - 7.5 min by linear regression (P = 0.014) and - 10.4 min by quantile regression (95% CI - 11.5 to - 9.2, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Our findings are consistent with improvements in trauma care within a mature trauma system, with shorter median time to computed tomography and lower 30-day mortality despite an aging population with increasing comorbidity. However, the specific drivers of these changes are difficult to identify, and future studies should explore how individual components of pre-hospital and in-hospital care contribute to trauma outcomes.

BACKGROUND: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the institutional trauma registry of Tan Tock Seng Hospital between January 2013 and December 2021. Patients presenting with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries were identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) coding. Demographics, injury characteristics, anatomical injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes including limb salvage, complications, and inpatient mortality were analysed. Comparisons between upper and lower limb injuries were performed using appropriate statistical tests.

RESULTS: Among 77,990 trauma admissions, 180 patients sustained PVI (incidence 0.23%). Median age was 36 years and 87% were male. Overall, penetrating trauma was more common (58.9%), but lower limb injuries were predominantly due to blunt trauma (68%), particularly road traffic accidents. Lower limb PVIs were associated with higher injury severity than upper limb PVIs (p < 0.001). Operative management was required in most arterial and venous injuries. Primary repair and endovascular interventions demonstrated excellent limb salvage, whereas bypass procedures were associated with lower salvage rates. Overall limb salvage for lower limb PVI was 88%, with an amputation rate of 10% and mortality of 3%. Most (93%) were functionally independent at discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: PVI predominantly affects young male patients and are commonly associated with blunt trauma from road traffic accidents. Despite significant injury severity, favourable limb salvage and functional outcomes can be achieved with timely multidisciplinary management. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary trauma care in optimizing outcomes following extremity vascular trauma.

item.title: Surface topography and nanostructural modifications for the prevention of bacterial infections.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma] [weak match]
Graziani G, Ghezzi D

Implant-associated infections represent severe complications in orthopaedics and trauma surgery, largely driven by early bacterial adhesion and subsequent biofilm formation on device surfaces. The increasing incidence of multidrug-resistant pathogens further complicates management and underscores the urgent need for preventive, antibiotic-free strategies. Surface functionalization of implantable metals has emerged as a key approach to inhibit bacterial colonization at the implant-tissue interface while minimizing systemic toxicity and selective pressure for resistance. This review provides a comprehensive and clinically oriented overview of two major surface-based strategies: micro/nano-scale surface patterning (non-releasing approaches) and nanostructured antibacterial metallic coatings (releasing or contact-killing systems). Surface patterning modifies topography, wettability, and surface charge to reduce bacterial adhesion or induce mechanical disruption of bacterial membranes. Although highly promising in vitro and not reliant on the release of antimicrobial agents, hence not inserting compounds with potential toxicity, current evidence indicates that patterned surfaces alone often provide limited and transient protection in vivo, where protein adsorption and complex microbial communities may mask topographical effects. In contrast, nanostructured antibacterial metallic coatings offer broad-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm activity through ion release and/or contact-mediated mechanisms. Advances in plasma-assisted deposition technologies, including magnetron sputtering, pulsed laser deposition, and ionized jet deposition, enable precise control over coating thickness, morphology, and ion-release kinetics, thereby enhancing antibacterial efficacy while preserving biocompatibility and osteogenic potential. Recent in vivo data support the durability and safety of thin nanostructured coatings, highlighting their translational potential. Although not-yet clinically available, due to challenges in clinical translation of biomedical devices, these strategies can build a new generation of antibacterial device, with efficacy targeted to the microbial community and to tackling biofilm. Comparative observations suggest that while surface patterning represents a valuable complementary strategy, nanostructured metallic thin films currently provide more robust and clinically relevant antimicrobial performance. Future research should prioritize standardized antibiofilm testing models, validation in complex in vivo settings, combination strategies integrating patterning and coatings, and the rational tuning of multi-metal systems to address heterogeneous microbial communities.

In this context, an older technique of minimally invasive cerclage fixation of the tibia is receiving renewed attention. The surgical technique has been adapted to contemporary cerclage systems and biomechanically evaluated for the first time. item.title: Overview and new developments in intramedullary and cephalomedullary nailing.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma] [weak match]
Hackl S, Weisemann F, Trapp O et al.

The primary objectives of osteosynthetic fracture stabilization are accurate fracture reduction, restoration of the anatomical axis and rotational alignment, and the provision of adequate biomechanical and biological conditions to support bone healing. In fractures of long tubular bones, these goals can be optimally achieved by intramedullary nailing, which provides long-segment internal splinting along the anatomical axis of the bone combined with locking screws to ensure axial and rotational stability. In addition, intramedullary nailing is a tissue-preserving technique, as nail insertion is performed remote from the fracture site, thereby minimizing soft tissue trauma within the fracture zone. The indications for intramedullary nailing include epiphyseal and diaphyseal fractures of long bones, selected metaphyseal fractures that can be stabilized using anatomically contoured nails, as well as reconstructive procedures such as the treatment of nonunions, corrective osteotomies, and arthrodeses of the lower extremity. A major advantage of intramedullary nailing is the high primary stability of the implant, which generally allows early functional rehabilitation. The resulting biomechanical benefits permit early full weight bearing and, in the treatment of fracture healing disorders, are associated with high rates of osseous union. Continuous improvements in implant design and instrumentation, together with the introduction of anatomically contoured reconstruction nails, are expected to further expand the indications and effectiveness of intramedullary nailing. This narrative review summarizes historical milestones, biomechanical principles, technical aspects, and recent implant developments in intramedullary nailing, with a particular focus on cephalomedullary nailing for unstable trochanteric and subtrochanteric femoral fractures. Special emphasis is placed on fracture reduction quality, implant selection, and screw positioning, as these factors remain the strongest determinants of fixation stability and clinical outcome.

The use of implants in the treatment of fractures evolved over the last decades. Until today, most implant designs are based on metallic alloys such as Titanium or stainless steel. External fixation remains a cornerstone of contemporary orthopaedic trauma and limb reconstruction surgery. While the biological principles for bone healing and regeneration established by Ilizarov continue to underpin modern practice, significant technological innovation has occurred over the past two decades. These developments have focused on improving construct stability, enhancing deformity correction accuracy, reducing technical complexity and improving the patient experience. Advances in hardware design have expanded fixation options and increased the adaptability of circular frames in complex trauma and reconstructive settings. Parallel developments in software have transformed deformity analysis, preoperative planning and correction execution through improved registration systems, virtual frame construction and cloud-based treatment platforms. More recently, remote patient support systems and automated strut technologies have sought to reduce the treatment burden associated with prolonged frame use. This review examines contemporary innovations in external fixation, focusing on developments in hardware, software, patient engagement technologies and automation. The available evidence is critically appraised and future directions explored. While many innovations demonstrate clear theoretical and practical advantages, robust clinical evidence remains limited for several emerging technologies. Nevertheless, the convergence of advanced engineering, digital health technologies and artificial intelligence is likely to fundamentally reshape the future of external fixation.

These implants are now used widely as a component of fixation in ankle fractures with a diastasis. The published results of their use in these injuries have shown that they are an effective method of treating diastasis of the ankle tibio-fibular syndesmosis with some evidence to suggest that they have a lower rate of malunion, fewer implant related complications, a reduced need for implant removal and in some trials better functional outcomes than screw fixation. Variations of these devices have also been used for fixation of lateral third clavicular fractures and acromioclavicular dislocations. Their use alone or in combination with plate fixation has been shown to be an effective method of fixation of lateral third clavicle fractures with a low rate of malunion and implant related problems. They have also shown to be an effective method of treatment for acromioclavicular dislocation, although there is still debate about the role of surgical treatment for these injuries. There is a broad consensus among orthopaedic and trauma surgeons, as well as infection specialists, that antibacterial coatings represent an important tool for both the prevention and management of fracture-related infections. Nonetheless, the choice of commercially available implants fitted with an antibacterial coating remains limited. Intramedullary nails with resorbable, antibiotic eluting coatings have been commercially available for over a decade. Although multiple case series have shown evidence of efficacy of antimicrobial orthopaedic implants, randomized controlled trials are still lacking and their uptake in everyday clinical practice has been slow. More recently, nails with galvanic noble metal coatings were introduced, with encouraging clinical results. The most widely used coatings with the longest clinical track record are silver coated joint replacement endoprostheses, which have been successfully employed in revision surgeries and in patients undergoing tumor-related procedures. Silver coated plates are on the verge of market introduction and will represent the first of their kind to be broadly available. Overall, adherent antibacterial coatings are showing beneficial outcomes in terms of safety and efficacy. Health-technology assessments show cost effectiveness, demonstrating that in higher risk patient populations, the additional cost of using a coated implant is significantly less than the cost of treating an infection. Regulatory hurdles remain high, especially in the USA, where, to be best of our knowledge, coated implants have not been approved yet. Driven by the clear clinical need, we anticipate a dynamic near future in this field, with progress moving toward establishing coated implants as the standard of care for appropriate patient populations and expanding the range of available coating solutions. Such developments will ultimately benefit patients, surgeons, and the overall healthcare system.

Large segmental bone defects remain a major challenge in orthopedic reconstruction because successful healing requires both mechanical stability and coordinated biological regeneration. Although autologous bone grafting remains the clinical gold standard due to its osteogenic, osteoinductive, and osteoconductive properties, its application is limited by donor site morbidity, restricted graft availability, and increased operative burden. These limitations have stimulated the development of scaffold-based regenerative strategies aimed at restoring structural integrity while promoting bone regeneration. Recent advances in additive manufacturing have enabled the fabrication of patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) scaffolds with controlled architecture, porosity, and mechanical properties that approximate native bone structure. This mini-review summarizes recent developments in 3D-printed scaffolds for the reconstruction of long bone defects, with particular emphasis on differences between non-biodegradable metallic constructs and biodegradable polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials. Porous titanium scaffolds demonstrate high mechanical stability and early osteointegration, making them promising for extensive load-bearing defects, although concerns remain regarding long-term stress shielding and permanent implant retention. Biodegradable ceramics and polymer-based scaffolds offer improved biological integration and controlled degradation, but often require further optimization of mechanical stability and biological augmentation. Composite constructs combining polymers, ceramics, or bioactive metals aim to integrate structural support with enhanced osteogenic and angiogenic responses. Despite encouraging preclinical results and emerging early clinical applications, current evidence remains limited by small patient cohorts, heterogeneous scaffold designs, and insufficient long-term outcome data. Future studies should focus on standardized scaffold designs, comparative clinical trials, and long-term evaluation to clarify the optimal role of 3D-printed biomaterials in the treatment of large segmental bone defects.

Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 162 (85%) patients in the iza-bren group versus 127 (66%) patients in the chemotherapy group, and haematological adverse events were the most common in both groups. For the treatment of haematological adverse events, 138 (73%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet-elevating agents, 28 (15%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet transfusion, and 18 patients (10%) in the iza-bren group received a blood transfusion. Two patients in the iza-bren group died due to treatment-related adverse events.

INTERPRETATION: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

item.title: Quantitative decision-support strategies to enhance emergency medical service accessibility in high-risk freeway tunnels.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [Prehospital] [weak match]
Jung S, Qin X

Crashes inside road tunnels often result in more severe outcomes due to spatial constraints that delay prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) access. Emergency evacuation facilities, such as cross passages and emergency parking areas, are critical for ensuring timely EMS response during traffic congestion caused by in-tunnel crashes. This study presents a quantitative approach to develop targeted strategies for enhancing such facilities to improve EMS accessibility in tunnels. Nationwide in-tunnel crash data from Korean freeways over a four-year period were analyzed, and the limited number of severe crash cases was addressed using SMOTE-based data augmentation to balance severity levels in the prediction model. A SHAP-based XGBoost classifier was applied to identify the influence of key features related to EMS accessibility and emergency evacuation facilities on crash severity. The results showed that crashes occurring more than 1 km from the tunnel entrance and EMS response coverage within a 10-15 km range have a significant impact on increasing crash severity. The presence of emergency cross passages, three or more lanes, emergency parking areas, and properly spaced CCTV installations were found to help reduce crash severity. Based on these findings, tunnels with particularly limited EMS accessibility were prioritized, and tailored facility improvement measures were proposed. This study provides quantitative evidence to guide cost-effective upgrades of tunnel emergency evacuation facilities, enhancing prehospital EMS accessibility and emergency preparedness. The proposed methodology can also support decision-making on implementing road tunnel safety improvement policies.

Utilizing a comprehensive hospital-based dataset in Karachi, Pakistan, and after addressing the issues of missing or inappropriate values via synthetic data generation, a Tobit regression (baseline) model was first employed in a corner solution setup. Harnessing 204,503 hospital-based motorcycle crash records (2007-2015) from Karachi (Pakistan), missing and inappaorpirate values were addressed through synthetic data generation. A baseline model and a finite mixture Tobit model (accounting for unobserved heterogeneity) were employed. The findings from the baseline model indicate that compared to mild/normal GCS (13-15) and SBP (> 89 mmHg), for crash victims with severe GCS (3-8) and severely low SBP (2-49 mmHg), the ISS significantly increases by 4.5249 and 7.8042 units, respectively. The finite mixture Tobit model identifies two latent classes of crash victims with dissimilar ISS patterns and varying relationships of key correlates with ISS, indicating that reliance on a standard Tobit model could lead to misleading inferences. item.title: Chest tube fixation strength depends on suture caliber and fixation technique rather than tube diameter: a biomechanical cadaver study.
item.description:
Eur J Trauma Emerg Surg | Core Trauma [General Trauma] [weak match]
Fricke JJ, Schöbel T, Meißner R et al.

BACKGROUND: Chest tube dislodgement remains a relevant complication in emergency, trauma, and intensive care medicine. In a previous biomechanical study, the Modified Johannesburg technique using Mersilene USP 1 demonstrated superior fixation strength compared with other chest tube fixation techniques. The present study aimed to determine whether suture size, suture material, and chest tube diameter influence fixation strength.

METHODS: A prospective interventional biomechanical cadaveric study was performed using fresh porcine thoracic wall specimens. A total of 320 load-to-failure tests were conducted under standardized laboratory conditions. Two fixation techniques, Modified Johannesburg and Purse String, were compared using two chest tube diameters (20/28 Ch) and four non-absorbable braided suture configurations: Mersilene USP 1, Mersilene USP 2 - 0, Silk USP 1, and Silk USP 2 - 0. Each experimental group consisted of 20 specimens. Specimens were tested in a uniaxial testing machine until construct failure. Force [N] and elongation [mm] at failure were measured. The experiments were videotaped, and the failure mechanism was analyzed.

RESULTS: The Modified Johannesburg technique demonstrated significantly higher pull-out forces compared to the Purse String technique (125.0 vs. 66.4 N; p < 0.001), as did larger suture sizes (USP 1 vs. 2 - 0; p < 0.001) and Mersilene compared to Silk (114.6 vs. 76.9 N; p < 0.001). Chest tube size had only a very small and inconsistent effect on pull-out strength. The predominant failure mode was suture rupture (94.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Chest tube fixation strength is significantly influenced by fixation technique, suture size, and suture material. The effect of chest tube diameter on fixation strength appeared negligible. The Modified Johannesburg technique, size 1 sutures, and Mersilene material provided superior biomechanical stability. Since failure occurred predominantly by suture rupture, the suture appears to represent the weakest link of the fixation construct.

item.title: Changes in patellar height following suprapatellar and infrapatellar tibial nailing: a retrospective comparative cohort study.

PURPOSE: Patella baja has been described after infrapatellar tibial nailing and may contribute to postoperative knee morbidity; however, whether the nail insertion approach influences postoperative patellar height remains unclear. We hypothesized that the suprapatellar approach would better preserve patellar height.

METHODS: A retrospective comparative cohort study included 114 tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing between 2016 and 2023, using a suprapatellar (n = 86) or infrapatellar (n = 28) approach. Patellar height was assessed using the Caton-Deschamps Index (CDI) on preoperative and final follow-up radiographs. The primary outcome was the longitudinal change in CDI (ΔCDI). Fracture union, complications, and reoperations were secondary outcomes.

RESULTS: The mean reduction in CDI was greater following infrapatellar than suprapatellar nailing (ΔCDI - 0.116 ± 0.173 vs. -0.011 ± 0.107; p = 0.001). After adjustment for baseline CDI and follow-up duration, this association remained significant (adjusted β=-0.055; 95% CI - 0.107 to - 0.004; p = 0.035), although sensitivity analyses showed attenuation after additional adjustment for sex. Fracture union rates were similar between approaches (93.0% vs. 92.9%; p = 0.987), with no statistically significant differences in complications or reoperations.

CONCLUSION: Infrapatellar tibial nailing was associated with a significant postoperative reduction in PH compared with the suprapatellar approach. This association persisted after adjustment for baseline CDI and follow-up duration but was sensitive to additional adjustment for sex. These findings highlight a potential relationship between nail insertion approach and postoperative PH but do not establish an independent effect of surgical approach.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective cohort study (Level III).

PURPOSE: The aim of this biomechanical study was to investigate the fixation stability of a small low-profile 2.7 mm variable-angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate supplemented with two additional independent cortex screws versus a traditional small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate in a standardized Sanders IIc fracture model.

METHODS: Sixteen fracture models cocomposed of three polymer blocks (fragments) each and simulating Sanders IIc intra‑articular calcaneal fractures were assigned to two groups. Group 1 (control) received a small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate, while Group 2 received a small 2.7 mm variable‑angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate with two additional independent cortex screws. All constructs were instrumented using prefabricated pilot holes and standardized screw configurations. Biomechanical testing was conducted implementing a 3‑point-bending setup and progressively increasing cyclic loading to failure. Angular interfragmentary movements were quantified via motion tracking along with cycles to clinically relevant failure.

RESULTS: Initial stiffness (N/mm) in Group 1 (65.2 ± 34.7) was significantly lower versus Group 2 (232.5 ± 48.6), p = 0.020. Although angular interfragmentary movements around the anteroposterior axis were significantly greater in Group 1 versus Group 2 (p < 0.001), Group 1 demonstrated significantly smaller angular interfragmentary movements around the mediolateral axis for the central-to-posterior and anterior-to-posterior fragment pairs (p ≤ 0.004), while no significant difference between the groups was identified with regard to the central-to-anterior fragment pair (p ≥ 0.377). Cycles and loads (N) to clinically relevant failure in Group 1 (3635 ± 176 and 92.7 ± 3.5) were significantly lower versus Group 2 (17433 ± 628 and 368.7 ± 12.6), p < 0.001. Failure mode in Group 1 involved plate deformation, whereas Group 2 failed through breakage or bending of the independent cortex screws.

CONCLUSIONS: Biomechanically, fixation implementing a small low-profile 2.7 mm variable-angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate supplemented with two additional independent cortex screws demonstrated stability comparable to, and in certain respects superior to that achieved with a small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate in a standardized Sanders IIc fracture model. However, the findings of this laboratory study do not establish an isolated benefit of the 2.7 mm plate itself, nor do they demonstrate clinical superiority or support alterations to postoperative weight-bearing protocols.

item.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
item.description:
N Engl J Med | Tier 2 Filtered [TBI] [weak match]

BACKGROUND: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.

RESULTS: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).

CONCLUSIONS: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

item.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.
item.description:
N Engl J Med | Tier 2 Filtered [TBI] [weak match]

BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.

RESULTS: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

item.title: Effect of blood transfusion on respiratory failure in severe trauma patients: A post hoc analysis of a randomized multicenter trial in Japan.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma, Haemorrhage, Systems/QI] [strong match]
Tanaka C, Tagami T, Fukuda R et al.

BACKGROUND: Severe trauma patients often need a large amount of blood transfusion including red blood cells (RBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet. The blood transfusion can cause serious transfusion-related adverse events including respiratory complications, however, the risks of blood transfusion in trauma patients have not been well documented. We evaluated the hypothesis that the amount of blood transfusion during the acute post-injury phase was associated with respiratory failure among severe trauma patients at risk of active bleeding using a database of a randomized multicenter trial.

METHODS: We used data from the Restrictive Transfusion Strategy for Critically Injured Patients (RESTRIC) trial, a cluster-randomized, crossover, non-inferiority multicenter trial conducted in Japan from May 7, 2019 to October 31, 2021 in Japan. The trial enrolled adult trauma patients transferred to the emergency department with severe bleeding or suspected severe bleeding and circulatory shock. All patients registered in this trial were included in this study. The primary outcome measure was the occurrence of respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. A logistic regression analysis on respiratory failure adjusted for sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), chest Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score, and the amount of RBCs, FFP, and platelet transfusions within 24 h was performed.

RESULTS: Of 417 trauma patients, 40 (9.8%) developed respiratory failure. Logistic regression analysis revealed that sex, chest AIS score, and platelet transfusion volume were associated with respiratory failure with 7 days after admission after adjustment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.300, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.113-0.794, p = 0.015, OR: 1.732, 95% CI: 1.267-2.367, p < 0.001, OR: 1.071, 95% CI: 1.021-1.122, p = 0.005 respectively). ISS, RBC, and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure (all p ≥ 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among severe trauma patients with severe bleeding or circulatory shock transferred to the emergency department, platelet transfusion volume within 24 h may be a risk factor for respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. In contrast, RBC and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure.

item.description:
Am J Emerg Med | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma, Systems/QI] [strong match]

OBJECTIVE: Secondary overtriage (SO) of isolated craniomaxillofacial (CMF) fractures overwhelm trauma centers and represent a significant resource burden while ultimately delaying patient care. The objective of this study was to implement an interfacility transfer protocol at a tertiary level 1 trauma center and review the preliminary utilization findings.

METHODS: A tertiary academic medical center adopted the protocol via the AgileMD pathway in regional referral centers. The protocol indicates the necessity of on-call specialist consultation based on a patient's clinical presentation. This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis for patients with isolated CMF trauma and AgileMD pathway activation over a one year period. The main outcome was transfer center activation.

RESULTS: The pathway was utilized 55 times for isolated CMF trauma patients in one year. The majority of traumas involved nasal bone fractures (52.7%) and were most often caused by falls (49.1%). On-call specialist consultation occurred 18.2% of the time - down from 100% of cases prior to guideline institution. The majority of patients (78.2%) were discharged with 40.9% follow-up, while 16.4% were transferred. These dispositions followed the guidelines 90.9% of the time.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first pilot study on the implementation of isolated CMF trauma interfacility transfer guidelines. The 81.8% reduction in on-call specialist consultation suggests a meaningful call burden reduction for surgical providers, while a discharge rate of 78.2% and outpatient follow-up rate consistent with pre-implementation levels reflects significant preservation of trauma resources. Broader adoption of similar protocols can further reduce SO, hospital costs, and wait times.

item.title: Harnessing the potential of response surface methodology-based optimized scaffolds in volumetric muscle loss repair in sprague dawley rat.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Kumar S, Iyer VA, Verma YK

Volumetric Muscle Loss (VML) is a complex tissue injury characterised by loss of tissue beyond the body's intrinsic regenerative capacity, resulting in impaired muscle regeneration and functional recovery. Limited cellular proliferation and poor in situ healing make VML one of the most challenging issues in tissue engineering. Conventional approaches of acidic gelling and use of artificial substrates compromise the structural integrity, biocompatibility and functional performance of tissue-engineered constructs. Moreover, the irregular geometries of muscle defects make surgical reconstruction technically challenging and often insufficient to achieve complete functional restoration. In this study, a novel porous scaffold containing collagen, fibronectin, and raloxifene (a cell-proliferative drug) was prepared for VML repair. The concentration of scaffold components was optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain an effective scaffold composition. The regenerative efficacy of the optimized scaffold was evaluated in a Sprague-Dawley rat model of VML. The results suggested that RSM-optimized scaffold significantly improved VML repair after 21 days (p < 0.05) in vivo. A prominent development of muscle fibre and deposition of collagen was observed. At molecular level, a significant increase in the expression of MyoD and STAT3 genes was observed in optimized scaffold group, suggesting enhanced myogenesis and tissue repair. The findings indicate that RSM may be utilized to optimize the tissue-engineered construct to improve VML repair.

item.title: General anesthesia is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation.
item.description:

INTRODUCTION: Anesthetic management of hip fracture fixation has two primary modalities: general anesthesia (GA) and spinal anesthesia (SA). Choice of anesthesia often depends on institutional protocols and the individual anesthesiologist, due to a lack of consensus guidelines. Most studies have conflicting evidence and focus primarily on elderly age as a risk factor, without accounting for frailty. This study investigates whether frailty influences the relationship between anesthetic modality and postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study queried the ACS-NSQIP from 2015 to 2020 for patients who underwent hip fracture fixation with open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws or intramedullary implant insertion. Patients were separated based on whether they received GA or SA. Frailty was evaluated using the 5-Item Modified Frailty Index (mFI-5). Patients classified as frail or severely frail were included. Multivariable regression adjusting for age, sex, ASA classification, smoking, and the comorbidities significant on univariate regression was performed. The outcomes examined were mortality, unplanned readmission, and overall complications within 30 days postoperatively.

RESULTS: This study included 24,401 patients under GA and 6193 patients under SA. On multivariable regression analysis, GA was independently associated with increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications among frail patients. Severely frail patients under GA had increased odds of unplanned readmission and all complications. When looking at both frail and severely frail patients together, GA remained a significant predictor of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications.

DISCUSSION: After controlling for ASA classification, our study found that frail and severely frail patients undergoing GA for hip fracture fixation had significantly increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications. Our findings suggest that SA may be safer compared to GA in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation. Frail patients that undergo GA may benefit from increased postoperative monitoring to help mitigate complications.

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) is effective for chronic subdural hematoma (SDH), but failure rates vary and risk prediction tools are lacking. This study developed and validated a machine learning (ML) model to predict MMAE treatment failure for SDH.

METHODS: We conducted an international, multi-institutional retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent MMAE for SDH between 2019 and 2025. The cohort was split into training and test sets, stratified by treatment failure, with all hematomas from each patient assigned to a single cohort to prevent data leakage. Multiple ML algorithms were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, with gradient boosting selected as the final model. The primary outcome was treatment failure, defined as rescue surgical evacuation or persistent/recurrent SDH requiring retreatment. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic. Patients were stratified into low-risk (<5%), medium-risk (5%-15%), and high-risk (>15%) groups using a priori clinically defined thresholds.

RESULTS: Among 692 treated hematomas in the test cohort, 64 (9.2%) experienced treatment failure. The gradient boosting model achieved an area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.803-0.902) before calibration and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.766-0.889) after isotonic calibration, with excellent calibration (Brier score, 0.053). Observed treatment failure was 1.6% (95% CI, 0.4%-5.7%) in the low-risk group (n = 124; 17.9%), 6.0% (95% CI, 4.3%-8.4%) in the medium-risk group (n = 516; 74.6%), and 59.6% (95% CI, 46.1%-71.8%) in the high-risk group (n = 52; 7.5%) (P < .001 for trend), a 37.2-fold difference between high- and low-risk groups.

CONCLUSION: This ML model stratified MMAE patients into risk groups with a 37.2-fold difference in treatment failure. High-risk patients had 59.6% failure, whereas low-risk patients had 1.6% failure. Risk stratification may improve patient selection and monitoring.

BACKGROUND: Injured females experience improved outcomes after component therapy resuscitation. We hypothesize that females <52 transfused with whole blood (WB) have improved survival, lower blood utilization, and lower complication rates compared with males and females ≥52.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis assessed Trauma Quality Improvement Program Participant Use File patients aged 18-90 transfused WB 1/1/2020-12/31/2022. Patients who were pregnant, transferred, anticoagulated, died <1 hour, had a blood dyscrasia, or severe head injury were excluded. Outcomes were compared between: female and male patients <52, female and male patients ≥52, and females <52 and ≥52, separated by injury mechanism. Univariate and multivariate analyses were applied, with the latter controlled for injury factors, race, medical history, time to hemorrhage control procedure, and complications.

RESULTS: 15 051 patients met inclusion. Male sex was associated with greater need for massive transfusion, higher blood product utilization, and acute kidney injury than females, regardless of mechanism (p<0.05, all comparisons). Among those injured by blunt mechanism, females received fewer of all individual blood component transfusions than males at all ages (all p<0.01). Females <52 with blunt mechanisms had equivalent mortality compared with males, whereas females ≥52 had decreased mortality (20.1% vs 24.2%, p=0.01). Compared with females ≥52, younger females had lower mortality (14% vs 20.1%, p<0.01) after blunt injury despite having worse injuries and receiving more component transfusions. These differences were not seen in patients injured by penetrating mechanism. On multivariable analysis, mortality was higher in males and females ≥52 compared with younger females (all p<0.01), regardless of mechanism.

CONCLUSIONS: After WB, being female and younger was generally associated with fewer blood transfusions, complications, and mortalities, but these differences were more pronounced in those with blunt mechanism. Females <52 demonstrated lower mortality compared with older patients. Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms of these findings.

Emergency general surgery (EGS) procedures are frequent and associated with higher morbidity than elective operations. Improving surgical quality for EGS patients is an admirable goal, which is fraught with several clinical and operational challenges. Surgeons must develop a skillset that is prepared to maintain clinical excellence and overcome the operational challenges that often prevent the initiation of new quality programs. This narrative review is from the Modernization of EGS short course at the 2026 EAST Annual Scientific Assembly. The session is divided into four parts highlighting specific EGS topics: hepatobiliary, alimentary tract, abdominal wall, and special patient populations. Topics were selected to provide current evidence-based approaches to commonly encountered pathological findings and notoriously challenging clinical scenarios. Included are expert opinion sections on the fundamental aspects of building a quality EGS program given by acute care surgery leaders with proven success.

Injuries from falls and their sequelae represent a significant source of morbidity and mortality. This impact is predominantly felt by patients with pre-existing health conditions and poor health. For these patients, comorbidities, frailty, use of anticoagulation, and other factors result in the development of severe injuries after relatively low-impact falls. Many strategies exist to counter the negative effects of falls-both thinking about how to reduce the incidence of falls by engaging in fall prevention strategies and techniques for reducing trip hazards or finding ways to minimize the potential impact of falls on vulnerable populations. These efforts can be combined to create local and regional fall-prevention networks, which have been highly successful and effective in addressing fall risk. This publication summarizes the contents of an American Association for the Surgery of Trauma's Virtual Grand Rounds that highlighted the epidemiology of falls, the effects of falls, and strategies for countering these effects at individual and locoregional levels.

BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health crisis, and craniofacial injuries are among the most common consequences. However, nationwide estimates of IPV-related craniofacial injuries remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of non-fatal IPV-related injuries using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS)-All Injury Program from 2018 to 2022. Cases were restricted to intentional assaults from a spouse or intimate partner. Craniofacial injuries were defined as injuries to the head, face, mouth, eyeball, neck, or ear. National estimates were generated using NEISS sampling weights, and rates per 100,000 population were calculated using US Census denominators stratified by sex, age, and race/ethnicity.

RESULTS: An estimated 888,279 emergency department visits were attributable to IPV-related injury during the study period, of which 58.3% (517,769 cases) involved craniofacial trauma. Female patients comprised the majority of cases (81.9%), experiencing an average annual rate of 97.6 per 100,000 compared with 20.4 per 100,000 for males. The highest rates were observed among women aged 20-26 (223.1 per 100,000) and 27-34 years (232.7 per 100,000). Black patients had the highest racial/ethnic burden (62.9 per 100,000), nearly four times higher than non-Hispanic white patients. Common diagnoses included internal injuries (28.9%), contusions/abrasions (28.0%), lacerations (17.4%), and concussions (4.2%). Most injuries occurred at home (85.2%) and resulted from being struck or hit (92.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore the need for targeted prevention, improved clinical recognition, and survivor-centered services addressing the neurological and psychosocial consequences of IPV-related head trauma.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single academic medical center.

INTERVENTION: None.

PATIENTS: Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation.

METHODS AND MAIN RESULTS: We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation.

CONCLUSIONS: A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

item.title: Pre-hospital care delays in trauma-related mass casualty incidents: a comparative international survey of high-income and low- and middle-income country perspectives.
item.description:

Alruqi F, Althobiani MA, Cole E et al.

BACKGROUND: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) place substantial demands on pre-hospital systems. Extended pre-hospital times are associated with adverse patient outcomes. The factors perceived as contributing to these delays are poorly characterized across different resource settings. This study aimed to identify and compare pre-hospital care providers' perceptions of factors associated with pre-hospital delays during trauma-related mass casualty incidents across high-income and low- and middle-income countries.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between May and August 2024. Pre-hospital care providers with experience of at least one trauma-related mass casualty incident were recruited globally via professional associations, alumni networks, and social media. The survey comprised expert-reviewed Likert-scale items and open-ended questions. Participants were stratified by national income level using World Bank classifications. Quantitative data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Open-text responses were analyzed using thematic analysis following the framework of Braun and Clarke.

RESULTS: Of 225 eligible responses from 54 countries, 158 (70.2%) were from high-income countries and 67 (29.8%) from low- and middle-income countries. Poor communication and geographical challenges were the most frequently cited delay factors, with agreement rates of 84% and 80%, respectively. Agreement that equipment inadequacy contributed to delays was reported by 75% of respondents from low- and middle-income countries compared with 46% of respondents from high-income countries. Thematic analysis identified eight qualitative delay themes: communication and coordination issues, resource limitations, infrastructure and scene access challenges, hospital capacity and preparedness, administrative and policy issues, training and preparedness gaps, security and safety barriers, and responder emotional burden and stress. Administrative and policy barriers were reported exclusively by participants from high-income countries. Responder emotional burden and stress emerged solely from qualitative responses and lacked corresponding quantitative items. Regular training and prior mass casualty experience were widely endorsed as optimizing factors, with agreement rates of 95% and 90%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-perceived delay factors showed similar patterns across settings, particularly communication failures, while differing in emphasis by resource context. Communication improvement, integrated into routine MCI training and operational planning, may represent a modifiable area for reducing perceived pre-hospital delays.

item.title: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients: a 9-year multicenter cohort study of clinical features, management, and 90-day outcomes.
item.description:
Crit Care | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma] [weak match]
Bidar F, Maamcha S, Tirard-Collet P et al.

BACKGROUND: Mucormycosis is a rare but life-threatening invasive fungal infection that primarily affects immunocompromised patients. Data on its presentation, management, and prognosis in the intensive care unit setting remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate 90-day mortality and to explore clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and immunological factors associated with outcome in critically ill patients with mucormycosis.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included patients diagnosed with mucormycosis and admitted to the ICUs of the Hospices Civils de Lyon between January 2014 and July 2023. Patients were identified through mycological records and hospital discharge codes. Univariable analysis and multivariable Cox model were performed to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 43 patients included, hematological malignancy and trauma were the most common underlying conditions (26% each), followed by solid organ transplantation (21%), and burns (16%). Cutaneous forms (49%) predominated, especially among trauma and burn patients, while pulmonary and rhinocerebral forms were mostly observed in previously immunocompromised individuals. The number of mucormycosis diagnoses increased nearly threefold over the study period, paralleling the implementation of Mucorales-specific polymerase chain reaction. Antifungal therapy was initiated in 39 patients (91%); first-line treatment was liposomal amphotericin B in 32 (74%), at a median maximum dose of 7.5 [3.5-9.4] mg/kg/day, and 12 (28%) received a combination therapy. The 90-day mortality was 47%. In the multivariable Cox model, older age, hematological malignancy, and a higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score at diagnosis were independently associated with mortality, while lower liposomal amphotericin B dosing was associated with mortality in univariable analysis. In eight patients without previous immunosuppression and uncontrolled disease, immune monitoring was performed and revealed decreased monocyte HLA-DR expression at 4556 [4194-6936] Ab/c, in favor of injury-induced immunosuppression. Among them, six patients received interferon-gamma as immunotherapy; four responded immunologically and survived.

CONCLUSIONS: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients is associated with high mortality, particularly in those with hematological malignancies. Polymerase chain reaction-based diagnostics may allow earlier detection, and immune monitoring could help identify high-risk patients, particularly in trauma and burn settings.

Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with increased trauma burden and poorer outcomes following open fractures. However, its impact on open upper-limb fractures remains unclear. This study examined whether socioeconomic deprivation influenced physiological status at presentation, Injury Severity Score and Gustilo-Anderson grade, time to surgical debridement, and early postoperative outcomes in patients treated within a regional major trauma network. We performed a retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained regional trauma registry at a Level I Major Trauma Centre. Consecutive patients presenting between 1 April 2014 and 1 April 2023 with open fractures of the humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, or clavicle were identified. Deprivation was determined using the postcode-linked 2019 Index of Multiple Deprivation. Patients without valid English IMD linkage were excluded. Outcomes were time to debridement, length of stay, 30- and 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, and postoperative infection. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, Injury Severity Score category, and Gustilo-Anderson grade. Of 297 identified patients, 291 were included. Patients from more deprived areas had poorer baseline physiological status, with ASA 3-4 status in 31.8% of the most deprived quintile compared with 10.0% of the least deprived quintile (p = 0.030). Gustilo-Anderson grade distribution differed across deprivation quintiles (p = 0.016), whereas Injury Severity Score category did not (p = 0.637). Time to debridement differed across IMD quintiles in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.017), but there was no linear association with continuous IMD decile after adjustment. IMD decile was not independently associated with length of stay, 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, or postoperative infection. There was no statistically significant association with 30-day readmission (odds ratio 1.196, 95% CI 0.979-1.480; p = 0.080), although the estimate was imprecise. Patients from more deprived areas presented with poorer physiological status, and the distribution of Gustilo-Anderson grades differed across deprivation quintiles. However, after adjustment for measured clinical covariates, there was no clear evidence that deprivation was independently associated with delay to surgery or worse early postoperative outcomes. Standardised trauma care may help mitigate socioeconomic differences in early outcomes after upper-limb fractures.

item.title: Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [General Trauma, Haemorrhage, Prehospital] [strong match]
Czarnecka Z, McCluskey S, Nadolski N et al.

BACKGROUND: Early identification of active hemorrhage (AH) is a critical challenge in trauma care. Narrowed pulse pressure (PP) has been associated with AH at the time of emergency department arrival; however, its role in the prehospital setting remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the utility of prehospital PP as an early predictor of AH in trauma.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multi-centre study (January 2017 - January 2020) including adult trauma patients at all three level 1 trauma centers in Alberta, Canada. AH was defined as either operative or interventional radiology hemorrhage control within 24 h of arrival, or transfusion of ≥ 4 units of packed red blood cells within 4 h. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to characterize associations between prehospital PP and AH.

RESULTS: 2177 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 68 (3%) had active hemorrhage. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had significantly narrower median prehospital PP (40 mmHg, IQR 29-52 vs 53, IQR 42-67; p < 0.001) and lower median systolic blood pressure (SBP; 111 mmHg, IQR 101-136 vs 138, IQR 122-156; p < 0.001). Prehospital PP demonstrated moderate ability to predict hemorrhage (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.67-0.79), comparable to SBP (AUC 0.74, 95% CI 0.67-0.81). Narrowed prehospital PP was independently associated with AH (odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79), reflecting a 51% increase in the risk of hemorrhage for each 10 mmHg the PP narrowed. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had worse outcomes including increased risk of ICU admission (63% vs 18%; p < 0.001), prolonged hospital length of stay (22 days, IQR 8-53 vs 7 days, IQR 4-15; p < 0.001), and increased mortality, although this did not reach statistical significance (18% vs 10%; p = 0.068).

CONCLUSION: Prehospital PP ≤ 45 mmHg identifies patients at risk for active hemorrhage and given its high negative predictive value, is most useful to rule-out patients without active hemorrhage in the prehospital setting. PP is a useful adjunct to support early recognition of hemorrhage in trauma. This is particularly relevant for trauma centres serving large geographic regions, where prolonged transport times delay definitive hemorrhage control. Its incorporation into the prehospital assessment has potential to help facilitate timely mobilization of hemorrhage control resources that actively bleeding patients require.

item.title: Comparative study of autologous bone graft and bone morphogenetic protein-2 for bone regeneration using a novel rabbit Masquelet technique model.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Yamamoto Y, Fukui T, Kumabe Y et al.

The Masquelet technique is widely used for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects; however, autologous bone grafting (ABG) is associated with donor-site morbidity such as pain and bleeding. Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) has attracted attention as a potential alternative strategy for promoting bone regeneration. Studies on direct comparisons between BMP-2 and autologous bone grafting within the context of the Masquelet technique are limited. The purpose of this study was to establish a novel rabbit femoral Masquelet model and compare the bone regenerative capacity of ABG with β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) loaded with BMP-2. A 20-mm segmental defect was created in the femur of 24-week-old New Zealand White rabbits and stabilized with a locking plate. The defect was filled with polymethyl methacrylate cement, which was removed four weeks later to induce membrane formation. The defect was subsequently filled with autologous iliac bone (ABG group) or β-TCP granules containing BMP-2 (BMP-2 group). Bone regeneration was evaluated 12 weeks after the second surgery using radiographic, histological, micro-computed tomography (μCT), and biomechanical analyses. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated satisfactory bone union in both groups, without substantial difference in union rate. Histological analysis showed cortical continuity and new bone formation in both groups. μ-CT revealed that the bone volume/tissue volume ratio of total calcified callus was significantly higher in the ABG group, whereas the tissue mineral density was significantly higher in the BMP-2 group. Biomechanical testing showed no significant differences in ultimate stress, extrinsic stiffness, or failure energy between the two groups. In this rabbit femoral Masquelet model, BMP-2 delivered with β-TCP achieved bone regeneration comparable to that of autologous bone grafting. These findings suggest that BMP-2 may represent a promising option for bone reconstruction using the Masquelet technique.

item.title: Oxidative stress in osteoarthritis: From mitochondrial homeostasis to targeted delivery systems.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [weak match]
Zhang Q, Li Q

Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic joint disease characterized by cartilage degradation, in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction play a pivotal role. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, driven by inflammation, metabolic reprogramming, and systemic risk factors, leads to mitochondrial damage, impaired mitophagy, and disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, forming a vicious cycle that accelerates OA progression. Although traditional antioxidant molecules show therapeutic potential, their rapid clearance from the joint cavity limits clinical efficacy. Recent advances in tissue engineering and smart delivery systems-such as ROS-responsive hydrogels, microspheres/nanocarriers, and exosome-based platforms-enable targeted, sustained, and on-demand drug release, offering new opportunities to restore redox balance and break the pathological amplification loop. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms linking oxidative stress to mitochondrial homeostasis in OA and highlights the design principles and application status of emerging delivery strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation for next-generation precision therapies.

OBJECTIVE: Although the application of autografts continues to be regarded as the gold standard for the treatment of peripheral nerve injuries, there exists a necessity for alternative grafting materials. BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are now the leading cause of major reoperation following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Patients are often frail and surgeries increasingly complex. We reviewed PFFs over two consecutive 8-year periods to analyse trends in incidence, management and outcomes to assess the evolving clinical and service impacts.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted using data from the Fracture Outcomes Research Database (FORD) and the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD) across two 8-year periods (2007-2015 and 2016-2024). Radiographic and clinical records were reviewed. Fracture classification, management, comorbidities and mortality were recorded and compared. A regression analysis was performed to determine co-morbidities that significantly increased the risk of 12-month mortality. In the 2016-2024 period, data on re-operations rates were recorded.

RESULTS: PFF increased from 189 to 320 across the two periods, totalling 509 patients. The incidence of Vancouver B2 fractures increased more than 1.5x, rising from 42/189 (22.2%) to 117/320 (36.6%) patients. Fixation remained the most common treatment across the two periods (75.1% and 63.4%), while revision arthroplasty was performed in 22.8% and 18.4% respectively. B2 fracture management changed significantly with fixation increasing (59% v 9.5%; p < 0.001) and revision arthroplasty rates decreasing (38.5% vs 85.7%; p < 0.001). Time to theatre improved (5-3.7 days; p = 0.028) and a higher proportion of patients returned to their pre-injury residence (30.2%; 57/189 vs 39%; 96/320, p = 0.068). No difference in mortality was observed at 30 days (2.6-3.1%; p = 0.796) or 90 days (5.8% vs 9.1%; p = 0.233) but mortality was higher at 12 months (12.2-20%; p = 0.028). ASA 4 patients increased (14%; 25/179; vs 29.1%; 82/282, OR = 2.526 (95% CI 1.54-4.14), p < 0.001). Re-operation rates were lower in the fixation group than in the revision group (12; 5.9% vs 8; 13.6%; p = 0.095).

CONCLUSION: The incidence and mortality associated with PFFs are rising within our unit, despite improved time to theatre and improved discharge outcomes. This trend may reflect a frailer cohort with higher ASA grades. BACKGROUND: Motorcycle crashes (MCC) account for a minority of vehicle miles in the United States, but their exposure-adjusted burden among trauma admissions is not well defined. The purpose of this study was to compare the injury burden of MCC versus motor vehicle crashes (MVC) using outcomes standardized by annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs (ACS-TQP) admissions from 2017 to 2023 was performed for adults aged 18-80 years admitted after MCC or MVC. Primary outcomes were admission, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality per 100 million VMT using Federal Highway Administration denominators. Motorcycle VMT was used for MCC, and light-duty vehicle VMT was used for MVC. Secondary outcomes included Injury Severity Score thresholds (≥16 and ≥25), severe head/neck injury, open long-bone fracture, ventilation, and return to the operating room. Relative risks (RRs) were estimated using binomial regression models with a log link.

RESULTS: Among 1,419,094 admissions, 334,310 followed MCC and 1,084,784 followed MVC. MCC accounted for 23.6% of admissions but only 0.71% of included VMT. Per 100 million VMT, MCC had higher rates of admission (236.4 vs. 5.49; rate ratio, 43.0), ICU admission (70.8 vs. 1.57; rate ratio, 45.1), amputation (5.06 vs. 0.028; rate ratio, 183.0), and in-hospital mortality (6.4 vs. 0.12; rate ratio, 51.6). Among admitted patients, MCC was associated with higher risks of open long-bone fracture (14.7% vs. 6.6%; RR, 2.22), amputation (2.1% vs. 0.5%; RR, 4.25), and in-hospital mortality (2.7% vs. 2.2%; RR, 1.20).

CONCLUSIONS: MCCs contribute a disproportionately high burden of severe trauma in the United States, with higher mileage-adjusted rates of ICU admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality than MVCs.

OBJECTIVE: The authors sought to identify plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1) cutoffs corresponding to a range of high positive predictive values (PPVs) for detecting intracranial pathology on CT and detecting pathology on MRI (when CT is negative) in patients who present to a level I trauma center for TBI evaluation with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores of 13-15.

Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (AUC) was performed to evaluate the ability of day-1 GFAP and UCH-L1 to discriminate CT+ versus CT-, and CT-/MRI+ versus CT-/MRI-. METHODS: Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized to naïve, polytrauma (PT), PT plus propranolol (PT+BB), PT with chronic restraint stress (PTRS), or PTRS plus propranolol (PTRS+BB) groups (n=6-8 per group). Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using an absolute log2 fold change ≥1.5 and p<0.05. Predicted pathways were assessed using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, and miR-125b-5p was validated by quantitative PCR.

RESULTS: PT altered 45 EV miRNAs compared with naïve animals, including suppression of miRNAs involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and erythropoiesis. Chronic restraint stress amplified this response, with 93 differentially expressed miRNAs following PTRS. Propranolol altered 12 miRNAs after PT and 43 after PTRS, increasing hematopoietic regulatory miRNAs, including miR-125b-5p, while suppressing several stress- and inflammation-associated miRNAs. Pathway analysis identified alterations in NOTCH, RUNX1, PTEN, thyroid receptor/retinoid X receptor, and histone modification signaling. CONCLUSIONS: Trauma and persistent adrenergic stress broadly remodel bone marrow EV miRNA signaling. β-Adrenergic blockade selectively reprograms these networks toward pathways associated with hematopoietic recovery, identifying EV miRNAs as potential mediators of posttraumatic bone marrow dysfunction.

INTRODUCTION: Circular frame fixation is a management method often used for complex fractures, or fractures with soft tissue compromise. Tibia fractures in older adults can be difficult to manage due to an association with osteoporosis, poor quality soft tissues, and a requirement for post-operative weight bearing to maintain function and independence. There is a paucity of evidence for the use of circular frames for tibia fractures in older adults. The available evidence suggests it is an effective treatment option, however, no study has compared treatment outcomes between older and younger patients.

AIM: To compare adverse events and outcomes between an 'older' cohort and 'younger' cohort of patients managed with circular frame for tibia fracture.

METHODS: The 'younger' cohort aged 18-50 and the 'older' cohort aged over 64 were identified from our institutional database. Injuries were classified using the AO/OTA and Gustilo-Anderson classifications. Data collection was retrospective and extracted from patient records. Adverse events were classified according to Paley as problems, obstacles or complications. Statistical analysis was performed, and significance set at p < 0.05.

There were significantly more females in the 'older' cohort, with a higher proportion having systemic co-morbidity (85% vs 24%) and diabetes (25% vs 3%). There were more smokers in the 'younger' cohort (33% vs 12%). There was no significant difference in rate of or time to union. The 'younger' cohort was more likely to require further procedures to achieve union. More patients in the 'older' cohort suffered a problem (30% vs 3%); pin site infection accounted for all problems in the 'older' group, and half the problems in the 'younger' group. The rate of obstacles and complications was not different CONCLUSION: Circular frame fixation is a suitable management option for 'older' patients who sustain tibia fracture, as there is no difference between rate or time to union when compared to a 'younger' cohort. 'Older' patients are more likely to encounter pin site infection and should be counselled regarding this. There is no difference between rate of more significant obstacles or complication.

item.title: Treatment and outcome of proximal femur fractures in a resource limited setting: a prospective observational study in rural Tanzania.
item.description:
Injury | Tier 2 Filtered [Orthopaedic] [weak match]
Eleveld AJ, Mtui GS, Hendriks TCC et al.

INTRODUCTION: Proximal femur fractures are a common type of fracture worldwide and are known to result in high disability and mortality rates. In resource-limited settings, these fractures are suspected to be an underreported problem. This study provides an overview of the different treatment modalities and outcomes of patients with a proximal femur fracture in rural Tanzania.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania. Between August 2019 and August 2020 patients admitted with a proximal femur fracture were included. Data on fracture type, treatment and outcome were collected up to one year after admission. Outcome included mortality, disability (Harris Hip Score (HHS), WHODAS 2.0) and Quality of Life (EQ-5D-3L, QoL).

RESULTS: Diagnosis: forty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 58-81). Thirty patients (30/47, 64%) sustained their injury due to a fall from standing height and eight patients were involved in a motor traffic accident. Eleven patients (11/47, 23%) sustained a femoral neck fracture, 24 patients (51%) sustained an intertrochanteric fracture and five patients (11%) sustained a subtrochanteric fracture. Five patients had additional injuries.

TREATMENT: eleven patients (11/47, 23%) received no treatment; 27 patients (57%) were treated conservatively; seven patients (15%) received an intramedullary nail. One Girdlestone (2%) was performed and one patient (2%) was referred to another hospital for operative treatment.

OUTCOME: The one-year follow-up rate was 96% (45/47). One-year mortality rate was 28% (13/47). Eleven patients (11/32, 34%) recovered to the disability level as reported prior to the injury (WHODAS 2.0). The HHS score showed a poor result in 21 patients (21/32, 66%; mean 62, SD 18). Seven patients had regained normal squat function. The QoL VAS at 3 months after admission was comparable to pre-injury reported general perceived health.

CONCLUSION: Most of the patients with proximal femur fractures are treated non-operatively and not according the current standard of care which is operative fixation or arthroplasty, resulting in limited functional outcome and high mortality rates. This data shows the importance of increased attention and the need for urgent improvement of fracture treatment and outcome in resource-limited settings.

Chronic wounds complicated by bacterial infections and poor tissue regeneration continue to present a major clinical problem in wound healing. This work describes a new hybrid scaffold made from zein-coated silver nanoparticles (Zein-Ag NPs) embedded in decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix (ECM). This scaffold has been designed to synergistically provide antimicrobial activity and enhance tissue repair. The Ag NPs were synthesized by chemically reducing silver nitrate with sodium borohydride and then coated with zein to improve the stability and biocompatibility of the Ag NPs. Upon evaluating the Ag NPs using dynamic light scattering (DLS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), it was determined that optimal Ag NPs were produced using a silver nitrate precursor concentration of 5 mM, which produced nanoparticles of ~35 nm in diameter. The fish skin ECM was decellularized using the optimized physical method. The Zein-Ag/ECM scaffolds exhibited strong antimicrobial activity in vitro against Candida species and bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, when tested using disk diffusion assays, and their controlled release of Ag⁺ minimized cytotoxicity. The biocompatibility of the material (hemocompatibility) was determined to be < 5% in vitro at 5 mM. Additionally, the material demonstrated support for the growth of fibroblasts in vitro. In vivo studies in rats showed that using the material to treat excisional wounds led to accelerated healing of the wounds, i.e., 90-95% healed by day 14, increased re-epithelialization, decreased inflammation, and improved organization of the collagen deposition in the wound site. Histopathology (using H&E and Masson Trichrome staining) confirmed this.

BACKGROUND: Temporary migrant workers may be particularly vulnerable to financial and occupational consequences after fracture. This study evaluated longitudinal income changes and socioeconomic outcomes following appendicular fractures in this population.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included temporary migrant workers in Kuwait aged 18-65 years presenting with appendicular fractures between January 2023 and January 2025.
